summary: Paraguayan dictator Francisco Solano López started the 1864-1870 war against Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay, tortured and executed his own elite, and sent child soldiers to die as the war killed most of Paraguay's population.

evidence.note: 1810-1811 independence from Spain and the junta set the start of the covered narrative
long segment on Francia's rule, isolationism and secret police
López born 1826 in the capital, raised on his father's estate
López family receives and trades enslaved Afro-Paraguayans
18-month European tour, France central, arms purchases and Napoleon III
1859 mediation of the Argentine civil conflict, his main diplomatic success
mixed arms purchases with no standard calibre, foundries dependent on imports
father dies 1862 and López becomes president
invasion of Mato Grosso (Brazil) after Brazil intervenes in Uruguay
seizes Corrientes and declares war on Argentina
San Fernando camp: torture and execution of brothers, elites and foreigners
child soldiers killed en masse at late-war battles

notes: Transcript says US minister Washburn was executed; historically he left Paraguay alive (legation staff were tortured). Transcript says the post-Francia coup was 1821, clearly a slip for 1841. Covered span starts at 1810 independence rather than Francia's 1766 birth, which is a passing line. Eliza Lynch birth year is disputed (1833/1835). Rehabilitation as national hero is a brief coda, so reaches_present is false.
